items.q: Why did Ramp build one shared coding agent?
items.a: Per-person setup wastes days and spreads best practice unevenly; one agent gives everyone a **solid baseline** that improves **for the whole company**.

items.q: How much of Ramp's code does Inspect write?
items.a: About **75% of code** written and shipped.
No; a strong baseline meant there was **no need to mandate it**.

items.q: How do Ramp engineers learn to use the agent?
items.a: Sessions are **public by default**, so they **learn by watching teammates**, no formal training.

items.q: What does a reviewer see on an Inspect PR?
items.a: The **conversation, tools used, screenshots and a verification video**, not just a diff.

items.q: What did a public bug thread produce?
items.a: A fix plus a **skeptic turned collaborator** within an hour.
Revering the **lone-wolf operator** instead of building with others.

items.q: What question should you ask colleagues this week?
items.a: **What have we been waiting to do** that we haven't done yet?
